The Finance (No. 2) Act 2010 is a piece of legislation enacted by the UK Parliament. It was developed as a series of revenue-raising measures to support the UK budget for 2010, as presented by the Chancellor of the Exchequer.

This was the second finance act in 2010, with the first being introduced in March and the second in July. 

Here are some key aspects of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2010:

1. Schedule 6 of the Act implemented charges on banks. It introduced a bank levy, which is a tax on the 'chargeable equity and liabilities' of a bank. This was to take effect from January 1, 2011.

2. It set out rules for taxes on alcohol, tobacco, and certain types of fuel. It also made provisions for environmental taxes, such as the landfill tax.

3. The Act included rules on the treatment of certain transactions for tax purposes. For instance, it set out provisions on how the tax laws apply to companies' loan relationships and derivative contracts.

4. Other aspects of the Act cover corporation tax, income tax, capital gains tax, value-added tax (VAT), stamp duty land tax, pensions, national insurance contributions, tax credits, and tax administration measures.

5. Schedule 11 of the Act pertained to anti-avoidance measures.

While the entire act is broad in coverage, its relevance and application may vary for companies, individuals, and situations. Legal professionals, financial experts, or tax advisors can provide specific guidance based on an individual's or company's context. 

Please note, some of the provisions of this Act have likely been updated or superseded by more recent legislation. For comprehensive and current information, it is always recommended to refer to the latest legislation, legal advice, and HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) guidelines. 

The Act as passed can be found from UK Parliament's official documents or other trusted legal resources. Always ensure you are referring to the latest and right version of the Act depending on the year under consideration, as there are more than one 'Finance Act' every year.
